content:
maya: Flagging a copy review for the modal that appears when the system falls back to a smaller model during capacity shortages. Current header: `Fallback enabled` and body: `Switching to a smaller model.` — feels terse and unclear about user impact.
ravi: Agreed. Users need to know whether data stays private, whether tokens/cost change, and if they can opt out. Also button labels matter: current buttons are `OK` and `Cancel` which is ambiguous.
bryan: Copy goals: be clear, low-friction, and avoid technical jargon. Propose three variants: 

1) Minimal: Header: "Using a fallback model" Body: "We're routing this request to a smaller model to meet capacity. Output may differ slightly." Primary button: "Continue" Secondary: "Don't fallback"

2) Contextual: Header: "Capacity fallback in effect" Body: "Your request will be served by a smaller model (faster, lower cost). Results may be less detailed. You can disable fallbacks in Deployment settings." Primary: "Proceed with fallback" Secondary: "Disable fallbacks" (link to settings)

3) Actionable + reassuring: Header: "We need to temporarily use a smaller model" Body: "To stay within latency and availability targets, we'll serve this request with a smaller model. Your data stays private and requests are logged as usual. Expect slightly different outputs and lower token cost. You can retry on your pinned model or disable automatic fallbacks in Deployment settings." Primary: "Use fallback for this request" Secondary: "Retry on pinned model" Link: "Fallback settings"

anna: I prefer option 3 for enterprise users but it's wordy. Maybe shorten the reassurance about privacy. Also we must avoid promising SLA-level guarantees. Replace 'stay within latency and availability targets' with 'to maintain responsiveness'.
design-bot: [automated] Current dialog: header=`Fallback enabled` body=`Switching to a smaller model.` buttons=[OK, Cancel] severity=info code=FALLBACK_NOTICE
ravi: Accessibility: screen-reader text should include the consequence (e.g., "Results may vary compared to your pinned model"). Button order should follow primary action first; confirm actions should be clearly named (no `OK`). Use aria-describedby linking to the longer explanation and ensure the modal receives focus on open.
bryan: UX micro-interaction: if the user has a pinned model, add a small line: "This request will use <pinned-model-name> if you retry." If pinned model isn't available, hide that line. Also show estimated cost delta if available like "~10% lower cost".
maya: For copy length compromise: header: "Using a fallback model" body: "To keep responses fast, we'll use a smaller model for this request. Results may be less detailed. Your data remains private. Retry on your pinned model or change fallback behavior in settings." buttons: primary="Use fallback" secondary="Retry pinned model" link="Fallback settings"
anna: Tone: neutral and explanatory; avoid fear words like 'temporary' and 'downgrade'. Use 'smaller model' rather than 'downgrade'.
ravi: Also telemetry: include the user's explicit choice in event payload (fallback_accepted/retry_selected/disabled). Add an optional checkbox "Remember my choice for this session"? Might need PM sign-off.
maya: Action items: 1) I'll update the mockup with the revised copy (the compromise version) and provide the SR announcement string. 2) Ravi, can you file the telemetry event and modal-a11y checklist? 3) Bryan, can you add the pinned-model conditional line + cost delta to the design token?
bryan: Will do. I'll mock the cost delta as placeholder text until infra provides real numbers.
anna: Approve to ship copy once PR contains the a11y text and button-labels changed from OK/Cancel. :thumbsup:
maya: Thanks team — I'll open the PR with copy + screenshot."
